correctness.rationale: Repaired final formal definition explicitly minimizes only over centrally symmetric CONVEX bodies, as the standard Estermann invariant requires. The original omitted convexity inside its displayed set quantifier and is literally false if arbitrary nonconvex symmetric supersets are admitted (e.g. R_n union -R_n has smaller area than the convex antipodal hull). Full corrected RESULT.md supplied with exact blob/hash guard. Independent proof review: alternating Steiner symmetrizations across distinct reflection axes preserve area, convexity, K-containment and centrally symmetric centers, whose projections converge to o; boundedness and Blaschke compactness yield a centered area minimizer. Symmetry plus width w gives support h(±u_j)=w/2 for axes perpendiculars, so R_n lies in n strips whose intersection is regular 2n-gon conv{±v_j}; reverse inclusion follows from vertices. Firey width-one formula gives area R_n=w²(pi/2-n/2 tan(pi/(2n))), hull area=nw²/2 tan(pi/(2n)), ratio and monotonicity and asymptotic. Independent bounded disk-intersection geometry checks n=3,5,7,9 corroborated areas to ~1.1e-6; numerics not universal proof. All odd n>=3 and w>0 only.

value.rationale: Regular Reuleaux polygons are canonical exact constant-width examples, and the classical Estermann outer-area measure is natural for this family. The finite/natural infinite-family classification gives an explicit optimal centrally symmetric containing convex polygon and exact unknown n>=5 area ratio, monotone convergence and two-term asymptotics. The particular value is useful as a benchmark contrasting the distinct inner Kovner–Besicovitch and Minkowski asymmetry measures. It is an elementary motivated exact special-family geometric fact, not a new general centering theorem, an irregular-Reuleaux extremal theorem, or merely a normalization change.

limitations: Only for regular Reuleaux odd n>=3, width w>0; no irregular-family extremality or uniqueness of center.
Original literal missing-convexity formal statement is false and was corrected in complete supplied RESULT.md.
Prior exact n=3 triangle and generic centering lemma are not new.
